The call enters `handleToolCall` in `pkg/okf/mcp.go`, which dispatches the `okf_create` case. There the arguments are pulled and validated: `resolveBundleDir` guards against path traversal on the bundle target, `getStringArg` enforces presence/length of `concept_id`/`type`/`title`/`body`, `ValidateConceptID` (pkg/okf/mutate.go) rejects empty/traversal/control-char/reserved IDs, and `getMutationStatus`/`getTagsArg` validate the remaining fields. It assembles a `*Concept` and calls `SaveConcept(bundleDir, c, SaveOptions{IsNew, AutoLog, AutoIndex, Actor:"agent/mcp"})`.

`SaveConcept` (pkg/okf/mutate.go) re-runs `ValidateConceptID`, calls `resolveInBundle` to confirm the path stays inside the bundle and isn't a reserved root file, then takes the cross-process write lock via `WithBundleLock` and runs `saveConceptLocked` inside it. `saveConceptLocked` resolves the full path, sanitizes metadata (`sanitizeConceptMetadata`, blocking YAML/frontmatter smuggling), and performs the bookkeeping (index + log).

The actual safe on-disk write is done by `atomicWriteFile` (pkg/okf/mutate.go): it writes to a temp file (`.tmp-okf-*`) in the same directory, `Sync`s it to disk, `Chmod`s, and atomically `os.Rename`s it over the target. So: `mcp.go:handleToolCall` → `mutate.go:ValidateConceptID` + `resolveInBundle` → `WithBundleLock` → `saveConceptLocked` → `atomicWriteFile`.
